newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Iraq in talks for post-sanctions oil deals - MEES.
newsitem.headline: Iraq in talks for post-sanctions oil deals - MEES.

text.p: Iraq is stepping up talks with foreign firms on oil exploration and production deals to be implemented once U.N. sanctions on Baghdad are lifted, the Middle East Economic Survey (MEES) newsletter said on Monday.

"Now that Security Council resolution 986 concerning humanitarian oil sales is fully operational, Iraq is stepping up talks with foreign oil firms regarding upstream E&P contracts to be implemented once the sanctions are lifted," MEES said.
It said Iraq was talking to Indian, Russian and Malaysian oil firms.

"MEES learns that upstream negotiations were held earlier this month between Iraqi oil officials and representatives of Malaysia's Petronas" over the Ratawi field in southern Iraq with recoverable reserves of around four billion barrels, it said.
"Moreover Petronas appears to have initialled an E&P agreement for Block 1 in the western desert," it said.

MEES said India's state-owned Oil and Natural Gas Corp Ltd was discussing with Iraqi authorities the development of the Halfaya field, located in the southeastern Iraq with recoverable reserves of around four billion barrels.

MEES said Russia's largest oil company NK LUKoil has completed a survey of the condition of surface facilities at the West Quma field which were badly damaged in the 1991 Gulf War which ended Iraq's occupation of Kuwait.
LUKoil earlier this month said it hoped to sign an agreement possibly in February with Baghdad to revive a stalled billion-dollar project to develop oil reserves in the field.
